avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inducer; significantly reduces nilotinib plasma concentrations and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue use immediately; do not co-administer with nilotinib

avoid_supplements.name: Rifampin-containing supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inducer; dramatically decreases nilotinib bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid all rifampin-containing products; consult oncologist before use of any herbal inducer

avoid_supplements.name: Grapefruit seed extract
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitor; increases nilotinib plasma concentration and toxicity risk
avoid_supplements.action: Eliminate from regimen; inform all supplement vendors of nilotinib use

avoid_supplements.name: Ketoconazole/antifungal supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitors; elevate nilotinib levels increasing adverse effects
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid unless prescribed by physician; require dose adjustment monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Garlic supplements (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 induction; may marginally reduce nilotinib concentrations
caution_supplements.action: Use low-to-moderate doses only; monitor for efficacy changes

caution_supplements.name: Milk thistle
caution_supplements.mechanism: Possible CYP3A4 modulation; limited clinical data with nilotinib
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; counsel patient to report any efficacy or toxicity changes

caution_supplements.name: Ginger supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential mild CYP3A4 effects; antiplatelet properties may increase bleeding risk with TKI
caution_supplements.action: Moderate use acceptable; monitor for unusual bleeding or bruising

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: Inhibits CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein; increases nilotinib bioavailability and toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Complete avoidance required; includes fresh grapefruit, juice, and related citrus (pomelo, Seville oranges)

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals
avoid_foods.mechanism: Substantially increases nilotinib absorption (fasting state is optimal); may elevate exposure beyond therapeutic window
avoid_foods.action: Administer on empty stomach; at least 2 hours before or 1 hour after meals

caution_foods.name: Cruciferous vegetables (high intake)
caution_foods.mechanism: Contain compounds that may induce CYP1A2; minimal effect on CYP3A4 but theoretical interaction
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption acceptable; maintain consistent dietary patterns for stable drug levels

caution_foods.name: Charred/grilled foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Heterocyclic amines may induce CYP enzymes; inconsistent exposure with high consumption
caution_foods.action: Consume in moderation; avoid charring/overcooking foods

caution_foods.name: Licorice (in foods/candies)
caution_foods.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 inhibition with excessive intake; sodium retention may complicate hypertension management
caution_foods.action: Limit consumption; significant amounts should be avoided

monitoring_notes: Nilotinib requires strict fasting state administration (empty stomach) and has critical CYP3A4-mediated interactions; monitor BCR-ABL transcript levels and QTc interval regularly, as interactions affecting drug concentration may alter both efficacy and cardiac safety. Patient education on absolute avoidance of grapefruit/grapefruit juice and CYP3A4 inducers is essential for therapeutic success.
